candidates: When removing dead code during cleanup, do not delete commented-out blocks that document available configuration options or alternative implementations (e.g., commented-out style-override branches, alternative curve or algorithm settings). These serve as in-code reference for future development and should be preserved until a deliberate decision is made to drop the option entirely.

When refactoring for cleanliness, avoid inlining or eliminating named intermediate variables that hold the result of a non-trivial call or computation. A named binding (e.g., `const direction = getDirection()`) makes the value inspectable at a breakpoint; the debuggability benefit outweighs the cosmetic gain of inlining the call at its use site.

In focused cleanup or chore PRs, do not remove code or functionality that is still under active investigation or that is explicitly planned for removal in a subsequent, larger coordinated PR. Confirm with the team that the code is safe to drop before including the removal; otherwise defer it to the appropriate milestone PR.
